remedies.text: Where the water route meets the interior walking route, at the last point at which a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk. Under the racks is a cold store cut into the rise, where unclaimed bundles have been stacked since the office opened.
remedies.why: The record's water is body.3234-806, a marsh fringe 56.5 m off at 11.46 m. There is no river at the dot and no bank to cut into, so the route is a water route and the store is cut into the rise.

remedies.text: Firm ground where clean water rises from a stone lip, at the last dry footing before the Helstrom approach.
remedies.why: The record's water is body.2442-1212, marsh deep at level 0.0, 93.2 m from the dot. There is no channel bank at the dot; the spring and the firm ground are what the ground gives.

remedies.text: Coming in from the fork, the standing water goes from black to clear over about a hundred metres. Frond smoke from the cookfires reaches the fork before the houses are in sight.
remedies.why: The dot stands 93.2 m from body.2442-1212 and no channel runs through it, so the approach is over standing water rather than up a channel.

remedies.text: A measured 46 m barrier gap flanked by 60-87 m ridges; firm lowland and drinkable spring water on the marsh side; a pond 77 m from the gate, from which the town's clay is dug.
remedies.why: The record's water is body.809-1686, a pond at 56.68 m, 76.8 m from the city dot. No Onkobra reach lies in Gideon's ring, so the founding names the pond alone.

remedies.text: The causeway runs straight at the keep for four hundred metres with wet ground on both sides. The whole length of it is watched from the terrace.
remedies.why: The record's water is reach.580-2263, a sloped rapid at 121.67 m, 193.8 m from the dot. There is no bog flanking the causeway, only wet ground.

remedies.text: On the waterside landing directly below the city, so a cart can be sealed at the wharf and opened in court.
remedies.why: The shed is Gideon's quay ward and Gideon's water is a pond, not a river, so the landing is waterside.

remedies.text: The upper water drops through eight ledges in a kilometre. Boats stop below the ledges and portage starts there.
remedies.why: The record stands on reach.836-841, a sloped rapid at 186.79 m, distance 0.0 m. That reach is not the Onkobra: the Onkobra is river.352-503, 1062.4 m away, and the name does not extend downstream because the chain below it is the attested Panther and Stormhold.

remedies.text: When the gorge floods it fills to within a few metres of the rim. The people who work it live on the wall, in cut chambers and built galleries above the worst water.
remedies.why: The record stands on reach.580-2263 at 0.0 m. The Onkobra is river.352-503, 1084.8 m away, so the gorge is its own and carries no Onkobra name.

remedies.text: Three and a half metres down in cold clear water, with its terraces stepping up to within a metre of the surface.

remedies.text: On the Lake road north of the city, at the last narrows before the water, where a cordon can be held.

remedies.text: A hole in the marsh south of the city which the water has not filled.

remedies.text: The Barsaebic Ayleids destroyed the tribe here and harvested its souls into the Remnant of Argon. The Hist did not die but slept. While it slept it was called the Dreaming Tree. At the end of the Second Era the souls were returned and the village was re-founded on its own ground, below the xanmeer Vakka-Bok.

remedies.why: The refuge is pinned at 2525, 4476, a ridge eight metres above the flood. There is no forty metre plateau in the frozen ground.

remedies.text: The Legion built on this rise because road and boat lane run together in the reach below and neither can go around it.
remedies.why: Same measurement: a rise over a marsh sheet, not a bluff over a gorge.

remedies.text: A deep, sheltered lagoon mouth on the Padomaic. It is the only landing on this coast that will take a foreign hull's draught. The Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here. The Saxhleel town grew landward of it.
remedies.why: The record's water is body.2727-2523, a swamp sheet at 3.76 m, 71.5 m from the city dot, and the harbour sample is the lagoon. The graph records no estuary here.

remedies.text: A lagoon with a landable stone shore and a road into the interior. The mangrove wall breaks here for more than a kilometre, the widest break on the east coast.
remedies.why: Same measurement: lagoon water and a road, with no river reach in the city's ring.

remedies.text: A drop in the water stops laden hulls, so inland cargo is unloaded, carried past the fall and loaded again. The town grew up around the carry.
remedies.why: The record stands on body.2783-2747, a swamp sheet at level 0.15, distance 0.0 m. No river is recorded under the fall.

remedies.text: A pillar of rock off the marsh edge, climbed for eggs by the Portdun Mont families for six generations. Someone else now holds the top. The climbing face takes 40 metres of rope.
remedies.why: The record's water is body.2444-2213, a swamp sheet at 1.34 m, 5.5 m from the dot. There is no headland and no open sea at the stack.

remedies.text: A vertical stack standing clear of the shore, with a mooring ring at the base and a worn climbing line up the outward face.
remedies.why: Same measurement: swamp water at the base, so the face looks over marsh rather than seaward.

remedies.text: A firm hummock on the open water's north shore, dry at the highest seasonal level and one boat-length from the channel.
remedies.why: The record stands on body.ocean at distance 0.0 m. The water it keeps marks on is the open coast, not an estuary.
